brief.subject: Fake passport help sites and a $106.8M debt relief ruling
brief.headline: FTC Targets Fake Passport Help Sites and Shuts Down Debt Relief Scheme Aimed at Seniors
brief.dek: Regulators act on government impostors in search ads, a debt relief scheme hitting seniors and veterans, and alleged register overcharges at Dollar General.
brief.lede: Scammers posing as the government are a top regulator target this week. The FTC sued a passport services operation, and a court shut down a debt relief scheme.

sections.heading: Fake Passport Help in Search Ads
bullets: The FTC sued GovAssist LLC, Entry LLC and Scott Zuckerman over an alleged government impersonation scheme.
The operation allegedly targeted people seeking passport services by posing as, or claiming ties to, the federal government.
Paid search ads were allegedly the hook, so a top search result is not proof a site is official.
The complaint also cites misleading promises and fake reviews, so glowing ratings alone shouldn't earn your trust.

sections.heading: Debt Relief Scheme Banned for Good
bullets: A federal court permanently banned the operators of an alleged debt relief scheme, at the FTC's request.
Seniors and veterans were the alleged targets, which matters if an older parent gets unexpected debt relief calls.
The operators allegedly impersonated banks, credit card companies and government agencies to seem legitimate.
On October 14, 2026, the court entered a $106.8 million default judgment against the corporate defendants.

sections.heading: Dollar General Sued Over Register Prices
bullets: The FTC and 20 states sued Dollar General over alleged long-running deceptive pricing.
Shoppers were allegedly charged more at checkout than shelf tags, price labels and ads showed.
The alleged overcharges cost consumers millions of dollars, so comparing your receipt to posted prices is worth the extra moment.
